methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native targeting technology gap closure signals grassroots capability-building through peer networks, potentially enabling distributed deep learning outside traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab creating workplace-focused AI training in a historically non-tech region demonstrates institutional capacity-building that could distribute deep AI fluency beyond NoVA concentrations.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's policy contradiction—promoting AI while localities resist data centers—reveals the infrastructure-capability paradox where NoVA's existing concentration deepens as other regions reject the physical requirements of AI economy participation.

signals.title: Google to invest millions for Virginia workforce development amid data center growth - WRIC ABC 8News
signals.signal_reading: Google's workforce development investment tied to data center growth suggests platform-led shallow adoption where corporate entities deliver AI capabilities rather than building indigenous expertise, creating dependency rather than agency.

signals.title: Appalachian Power sees ‘explosive’ growth from data centers, other big customers
signals.signal_reading: Appalachian Power's explosive data center demand in traditionally underserved regions raises stakes for infrastructure inequality—these areas may host AI infrastructure while lacking workforce capability to capture economic value, deepening extraction patterns.
